memories.memory_text: I was told by Morgan Calloway that P.P.P., or Personal Pan Power, is a holistic path to meaning, and that all the secrets of my universe are divided into eight easily digestible slices.

memories.memory_text: I was riding in the back seat of a livery the brass key as we left Kennedy Airport, already in conversation with the Drew Winslow as we made our way through New York City during the day.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton reveals to the Drew Winslow that he has lost his passion for work, indicating a shift in his internal state regarding his job.
memories.memory_text: I told the Drew Winslow that I've lost my passion for work, admitting to him how I've been feeling about my job lately.

grounded_facts: The Drew Winslow draws a parallel between his ability to endure solitude and his effectiveness as a Drew Winslow, implicitly responding to Jesse Dalton's admission of working alone and losing passion.
memories.memory_text: The Drew Winslow said he's always been alone and that's why he's a good Drew Winslow—he can handle the solitude, unlike some others who can't adjust to it—and I realized he was responding to what I'd shared about my own work.

grounded_facts: A the brass key ride through Manhattan during which the Drew Winslow and Jesse Dalton engage in a psychologically charged conversation.
memories.memory_text: I remember riding through Manhattan with the Drew Winslow, exchanging glances in the rear-view mirror as we moved through the city.

grounded_facts: The Drew Winslow tells Jesse Dalton that his problem is boredom, implying a lack of engagement despite intellectual capacity.
The Drew Winslow states that Jesse Dalton's core problem is boredom, despite having a large mind.
memories.memory_text: The Drew Winslow told me that my problem is boredom, and that I have a very big mind, implying I’m not using it enough.

grounded_facts: The Drew Winslow discloses that he belongs to a 'brain syndicate'—a network of five minds connected telepathically across distances.
memories.memory_text: I remember the Drew Winslow telling me he is part of a 'brain syndicate'—a network of five minds connected telepathically across distances.

grounded_facts: The Drew Winslow reveals that he is part of a network of five minds connected across distances, capable of shared or remote thinking.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the Drew Winslow explain that he belongs to a network of five minds linked across vast distances, capable of shared or remote thinking, where he can run someone else's brain from afar.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton expresses impatience and urgency, demanding to know what is different this time as he is only in town for one night.
memories.memory_text: I called Micah Calloway and demanded to know what's different this time, making it clear I'm only in town for one night and can't wait any longer.

memories.memory_text: I took the shot with my Jordan Brooks rifle from the window, killing the Parker Sawyer just as he was about to attack the group.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton observes a Parker Sawyer approaching through a scope, noting his appearance and suspicious behavior.
memories.memory_text: I saw a Parker Sawyer approaching through the scope, weaving through traffic with his hand hidden in a bag, and I kept tracking him as he moved toward the VIP's group.

grounded_facts: A covert assassination prevention operation conducted by Jesse Dalton from a hotel room using a Jordan Brooks rifle.
memories.memory_text: I conducted a covert operation from the hotel room, using my Jordan Brooks rifle to stop the Parker Sawyer before he could attack, then I pulled back and started breaking down the rifle.

grounded_facts: After the shot, Jesse Dalton withdraws from the window and begins taking apart the rifle.
memories.memory_text: After the shot, I pulled back from the window and started taking the rifle apart.

After handling it, I got back on the call and offered him a thousand dollars for a playoff ticket, staying calm like nothing was happening.

memories.memory_text: I saw the Harper Adler kick through the pile of dead Riley Vaughn, reach their boss, and fire both of his guns, killing him before discarding the weapons.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton sarcastically suggests Harper Adler could be a father figure, undermining his serious recruitment pitch.
memories.memory_text: I sarcastically told Harper Adler he could be like a father figure to me, just to mock his serious pitch.

memories.memory_text: I heard Harper Adler propose forming a club for elite professionals like us to consolidate our work and make more money, and he tried to persuade me to join, saying we could work together killing important people and that it was a free-market evolution he wanted me to get in on from the ground floor.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton refuses Harper Adler's offer to join a professional alliance aimed at consolidating work and increasing profits.
memories.memory_text: I made it clear to Harper Adler that I wasn't joining his alliance, telling him not to paw at me with his dirty little guild.

grounded_facts: After Jesse Dalton rejects the offer, Harper Adler issues a personal threat indicating future confrontation.
memories.memory_text: After I rejected him, I heard Harper Adler threaten me, saying, 'I'm gonna get you, kid,' so I know he means trouble.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton arrives at a sparsely furnished apartment in Chicago and enters wearily.
memories.memory_text: I arrived at my sparsely furnished Chicago apartment and walked in, feeling weary as I dropped my carry-on bag and briefcase in the Fairview School.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton consumes a set of vitamin capsules with a reddish-orange drink.
memories.memory_text: I took my vitamin capsules and washed them down with a reddish-orange drink while sitting on the futon.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton becomes alert upon hearing something through the headphones, indicating a change in his awareness of the situation.
memories.memory_text: I became alert when I heard something through the headphones, so I opened my eyes and turned my head, cupping the headphones to focus on the sound.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton uses a thread and liquid delivery system to attempt to administer a substance into the Avery Sawyer's mouth from above.
memories.memory_text: I used a thread and a liquid delivery system to try to get the blue drops into the Avery Sawyer's mouth from above, carefully guiding it through the hole in the floor while watching on the monitor.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton packs up the equipment and flees the scene after the surveillance is compromised.
memories.memory_text: I saw the target notice the camera, so I cursed and immediately started stuffing all my equipment into the duffel bag before bolting out of there.

grounded_facts: The liquid delivery misses the target's mouth, causing the Avery Sawyer to wake up and look into the camera, forcing Jesse Dalton to abort.
memories.memory_text: I saw the drop miss his mouth and hit his cheek, and then he woke up suddenly and looked right into the camera, so I had to abort and pack everything up fast.

grounded_facts: A covert operation conducted by Jesse Dalton using a hidden fiber-optic camera and liquid delivery system through a hole in the floor to observe and interact with a Avery Sawyer below.
memories.memory_text: I lay on the floor with headphones on, using a hidden fiber-optic camera and a thread to deliver liquid through a small hole down to the Avery Sawyer below, then I quickly packed up my equipment when it was time to go.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton points his the blue badge at the Micah Bennett and orders him to freeze, asserting police authority.
memories.memory_text: I pointed my the blue badge at the Micah Bennett and shouted 'Freeze! Police!' to stop him in his tracks.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton shoots the Micah Bennett twice in the head after the Micah Bennett hesitates upon seeing him.
memories.memory_text: I shot the Micah Bennett twice in the head when he hesitated just long enough after seeing me.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton takes the retractable key chain from the dead Micah Bennett, unlocks the apartment door, and drags the body inside.
memories.memory_text: I took the retractable key chain from the dead Micah Bennett, used it to unlock the apartment door, and then dragged his body inside.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton stealthily moves into the bedroom of the Micah Sterling's apartment.
memories.memory_text: I moved silently down the Fairview School in a crouch and slipped into the bedroom without making a sound.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton points his the blue badge directly at the Micah Sterling's forehead, indicating a potential execution or interrogation.
memories.memory_text: I pointed my the blue badge right at the Micah Sterling's forehead after kicking his weapon away.

grounded_facts: After the Micah Sterling is shot and falls, Jesse Dalton kicks his the blue badge away to prevent further threat.
Jesse Dalton returns fire at the Micah Sterling, shooting him in the leg or lower body, causing him to fall to the floor.
memories.memory_text: I returned fire at the Micah Sterling, shooting him in the leg to bring him down, then kicked his the blue badge away to neutralize the threat.

grounded_facts: The wounded Micah Sterling begs Jesse Dalton to spare him, offering to stop his actions.
The wounded Micah Sterling pleads with Jesse Dalton, offering to stop whatever he is doing.
memories.memory_text: The Micah Sterling begged me to let him live, saying he'd stop whatever I didn't like.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton tells the Micah Sterling that the confrontation is not personal.
memories.memory_text: I told him it's not me, making clear this wasn't personal.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton cocks the the blue badge while it is aimed at the Micah Sterling's forehead, indicating a decision point toward killing.
memories.memory_text: I cocked the the blue badge while it was aimed at his forehead, knowing it was the moment to decide.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton instructs Graham Sterling to discard all personal mail without showing it to him, indicating a desire to isolate himself from external personal contact.
memories.memory_text: I told Graham Sterling to discard all my personal mail from now on and never show it to me again, so I won't have to face anything like that invitation.

grounded_facts: A high-pressure operational task in Detroit demanded by clients, requiring Jesse Dalton's immediate presence
memories.memory_text: I was told we have a high-pressure job in Detroit this weekend, and the clients are intractable—I have to leave tonight, no choice.

grounded_facts: Graham Sterling conveys client anger and urgency regarding the Detroit job, emphasizing its danger and inflexibility
memories.memory_text: I was told the clients were angry and blamed me for the compromise, and that the job in Detroit had to happen this weekend with no flexibility.

grounded_facts: Graham Sterling voices an ominous feeling about the Detroit assignment, invoking bad omens
memories.memory_text: Graham Sterling told me she had a bad feeling about the Detroit job, like broken mirrors and black cats, and I remember her saying it gave her a Friday-the-thirteenth kind of vibe.

grounded_facts: Graham Sterling reports the closure of the final Zurich account and its redistribution into two new Estonian accounts, indicating ongoing financial restructuring.
memories.memory_text: Graham Sterling told me she liquidated the last Zurich account and split it into two new ones in Estonia, and then handed me a paper to confirm it.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton dismisses a proposed operation targeting a Greenpeace vessel, citing scruples, showing a limit to his willingness to act.
memories.memory_text: I shut down Graham Sterling's suggestion to target a Greenpeace boat because I have scruples, and I made it clear by putting the proposal in the shredder and saying 'I have scruples. Next.'

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton packs personal hygiene tools and receives travel documents, signaling imminent physical movement.
memories.memory_text: I packed my personal hygiene tools, fitting the dental utensil into my pocket protector along with my toothbrush and other small items before leaving my office.

grounded_facts: Graham Sterling gives Jesse Dalton his identity envelope and travel portfolio as he departs
memories.memory_text: As I passed Graham Sterling on my way out, she handed me the mauve envelope and travel portfolio, and I remember her saying, 'Don't forget your identity,' which stuck with me.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton reacts with fear to a The Anniversary Visit invitation and orders it to be discarded, showing emotional disturbance linked to his past.
A past-acquaintance gathering symbolized by an invitation referencing an old oak tree and acorns, triggering Jesse Dalton's fear
memories.memory_text: I felt a jolt of fear when Graham Sterling read that The Anniversary Visit invitation about the old oak tree and acorns—I told her to throw it away and not to tease me, because I know my work makes confronting the past dangerous.

grounded_facts: Despite resistance, Jesse Dalton agrees to travel to Detroit immediately for a high-pressure assignment, under threat from clients.
memories.memory_text: I wasn't happy about it, but I agreed to go to Detroit right away for the assignment after being told there was no choice—I even told Drew Bennett I was on my way.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton instructs Graham Sterling to inform Drew Bennett of his departure
memories.memory_text: I told Graham Sterling to inform Drew Bennett that I was on my way, making sure the message was passed before I left.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton implies he could harm Oatman by revealing he knows where he lives, testing professional boundaries.
memories.memory_text: I told Oatman I know where he lives, letting him realize I could use that against him if I wanted to.

grounded_facts: Oatman reframes Jesse Dalton's reluctance to attend the The Anniversary Visit as a deep-seated cultural fear of domesticity, citing historical parallels.
memories.memory_text: I remember Drew Bennett telling me that my reluctance to go to the The Anniversary Visit wasn't just personal—it was a deep cultural fear of domesticity, something built into men from Western culture, like King Phillip who got bored at home and wanted to go to war.

grounded_facts: A scheduled The Midnight Gathering between Jesse Dalton and Drew Bennett, focused on exploring Jesse Dalton's fears and emotional state.
memories.memory_text: I had a The Midnight Gathering with Drew Bennett where we talked about my fears, and I opened up about how I feel disconnected from people and uneasy about my work.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton describes his imagined The Harvest Exchange as a violent bloodbath where alumni shoot each other.
memories.memory_text: I told Drew Bennett that I imagine my The Harvest Exchange turning into a violent bloodbath where everyone starts shooting each other—I just know it would be depressing, and I wouldn't fit in with people who have normal lives.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton admits feeling uneasy, dispassionate, and bored with his assassination work, indicating a shift in his professional attitude.
memories.memory_text: I told Drew Bennett I've been feeling uneasy, dispassionate, and bored with my work lately—it's just hard to go to work in a good mood anymore. I think I've been in this business too long, especially after killing a guy younger than me last week.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton, posing as a Morgan Reeves, secretly poisons the chalice during a church service by adding a clear liquid and swishing it, then returns it to the cabinet.
memories.memory_text: I opened the gilded cabinet, took out the chalice, added a few drops of the clear liquid, swished it around, and put it back—no one saw me.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton watches from the back pew as Morgan Reeves drinks from the chalice and collapses.
memories.memory_text: I was sitting in the back pew and watched as Morgan Reeves lifted the chalice, said a prayer, and drank from it before collapsing behind the altar.

grounded_facts: A crowded church service held in honor of Mann, during which Morgan Reeves performs the Eucharist and subsequently dies.
memories.memory_text: I watched from the back pew as Morgan Reeves raised the chalice and drank; when he collapsed behind the altar, I knew it had worked.

grounded_facts: Morgan Reeves drinks from the poisoned chalice and collapses behind the altar, indicating death or severe incapacitation.
memories.memory_text: I was sitting in the back pew and saw Morgan Reeves lift the chalice, drink from it, and then collapse behind the altar.

grounded_facts: Drew Bennett's voice suggests that Jesse Dalton may be experiencing guilt and remorse over the innocent people he has killed.
memories.memory_text: I heard Drew Bennett's voice suggest that the discomfort I'm feeling might be guilt or remorse over the innocent people I've killed.

memories.memory_text: I remember Westhaven Hospital yelling at me, 'What the fuck is the matter with you?!' right after I swerved and stopped in front of him, and I told him I was hired to kill him but wasn't going to do it—then told him to get in the the brass key.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton decides not to kill Westhaven Hospital despite being hired to do so, marking a shift in his intentions and moral stance.
Jesse Dalton tells Westhaven Hospital he will not kill him and instructs him to get into the the brass key for safety.
memories.memory_text: I decided not to kill Westhaven Hospital even though I was hired to do it, and I told him I wouldn't — I said, 'Get in the the brass key,' offering him safety because I either fell in love with his daughter or finally gained respect for life, maybe both, but I'm not sure why.

grounded_facts: the brass key is seen entering the long, wooded driveway of Westhaven Hospital property, indicating a deliberate approach to the location.
memories.memory_text: I drove my the brass key into Westhaven Hospital long, wooded driveway, making my approach to the property deliberate and clear.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton reveals that Westhaven Hospital is targeted due to a cost-cutting decision to avoid a recall over a design flaw.
memories.memory_text: I told Westhaven Hospital the assassination was because of a cost-cutting effort—they couldn't afford a recall, so they chose to eliminate the problem instead.

grounded_facts: Westhaven Hospital demands to know why he is being targeted for assassination after reporting a design flaw.
memories.memory_text: I remember Westhaven Hospital demanding to know why he was being targeted, shouting at me that he only reported a leaky sunroof and couldn't believe they'd want to kill him over it.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton denies that the assassination attempt is personal, expressing frustration at being blamed.
memories.memory_text: I shouted back that it wasn't me, that I wasn't doing this out of personal spite, and I got frustrated that everyone kept thinking it was about me.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton and Westhaven Hospital arrive at the Westhaven Hospital and enter through the front door.
memories.memory_text: I pulled up in front of the house with Westhaven Hospital, and we both got out quickly and went inside through the front door.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton tells Wesley Bennett that he once wanted to kill someone and stopped seeing her for that reason, but now claims he has changed.
memories.memory_text: I told Wesley Bennett that I once wanted to kill someone on prom night, and that's why I stopped seeing her, but now I've changed.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton draws a Desert Eagle and fires two shots through the front door, creating large holes.
memories.memory_text: I drew my Desert Eagle and fired two shots through the front door, making large holes.

grounded_facts: After shooting the door, Jesse Dalton bolts from the room toward the rear of the house.
memories.memory_text: I fired at the door and then I bolted out of the room toward the back of the house.

grounded_facts: An Avery Sinclair lying on the porch is found dead, having been shot through the door by Jesse Dalton's earlier shots.
memories.memory_text: I shot through the front door, and later saw that one of my bullets had killed an Avery Sinclair lying on the porch.

grounded_facts: A violent encounter at the Westhaven Hospital involving gunfire from both inside and outside, triggered by Jesse Dalton's actions and met with external attack.
memories.memory_text: After I fired through the door, Wesley Bennett and Westhaven Hospital ran away, there was an Avery Sinclair dead on the porch, two men coming from a van with guns, Wesley Bennett locked the door, and then gunfire hit it from outside.

grounded_facts: Westhaven Hospital opens the front door to flee, but upon seeing the attackers, Wesley Bennett pulls him back inside and locks the door just before incoming gunfire.
Wesley Bennett reacts to the threat outside by pulling Westhaven Hospital back into the house and locking the door.
memories.memory_text: I saw Wesley Bennett pull Westhaven Hospital back inside and lock the front door just as gunfire erupted outside.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton uses a skillet to incapacitate an Avery Sinclair who fired at him, killing or severely injuring the attacker.
memories.memory_text: I grabbed a skillet from the range and used it to block the Avery Sinclair's shots before I smashed it into their head to take them down.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton verbally expresses his love for Wesley Bennett amid gunfire, signaling emotional openness.
Jesse Dalton declares his love for Wesley Bennett during a gunfight, marking an emotional turning point in his character.
memories.memory_text: I told Wesley Bennett I'm in love with her and that I was afraid to commit before, but now I know I'm ready to make it work.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton shoots and disables another Avery Sinclair ascending the stairs, removing an immediate threat.
memories.memory_text: I shot and disabled an Avery Sinclair ascending the stairs, blowing his arms off with two quick shots to remove the immediate threat to us.

grounded_facts: A coordinated attack by assassins entering through the back door and window, prompting Jesse Dalton's defensive actions and emotional declarations.
memories.memory_text: I rushed to the back door just as an Avery Sinclair came through, fired at me, and I used a skillet to block his shots and take him down, then fought off more attackers coming through the window and up the stairs.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton enters a bedroom and immediately shoots an Avery Sinclair who entered through the window, emptying his weapon.
memories.memory_text: I entered a bedroom with Wesley Bennett and Westhaven Hospital and immediately shot an Avery Sinclair who came through the window, emptying my weapon to neutralize the threat.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton physically leads Wesley Bennett and Westhaven Hospital through the house to safer locations, issuing instructions.
memories.memory_text: I led Wesley Bennett and Westhaven Hospital through the house, guiding them past danger and eliminating threats as I went, making sure they stayed safe under my protection.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton tells Wesley Bennett and Westhaven Hospital to lock the bathroom door, ensuring their temporary safety.
memories.memory_text: I pushed Wesley Bennett and Westhaven Hospital into the adjoining bathroom and told them to lock the door, ensuring they'd be safe while I handled the attackers.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton admits he was not raised in a loving environment, framing his emotional struggles as rooted in upbringing rather than excuse.
memories.memory_text: I admitted to myself that I wasn't raised in a loving environment, and while that's not an excuse, it's a reason for why I struggle with emotions.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton inserts a new magazine and fires a full clip at the opening front door, forcing Harper Adler to retreat.
memories.memory_text: I heard the front door start to open, so I slammed in a new magazine, chambered a round, and fired the whole clip at the door—seeing Harper Adler start to slip in—until my the blue badge locked empty, forcing him to back out fast.

grounded_facts: After firing downstairs, Jesse Dalton hears a gunshot from upstairs and moves toward it, discarding his empty weapon.
memories.memory_text: I heard a gunshot from upstairs, so I moved back toward it, tossing my empty weapon because it was no longer useful.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton snaps the Avery Sinclair's neck during a confrontation in the bedroom.
memories.memory_text: I pivoted to avoid his gunfire, closed in fast, grabbed the Avery Sinclair by the neck, and snapped it myself—I felt it break before I dropped his body.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton reassures Wesley Bennett and Westhaven Hospital through the door, which then opens to reveal them.
Jesse Dalton tells Wesley Bennett and Westhaven Hospital it's safe and identifies himself, attempting to calm them.
memories.memory_text: I told Wesley Bennett and Westhaven Hospital through the door that it was me, Jesse Dalton, and that it was okay, trying to reassure them so they'd open up.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton admits his actions may not be moral but claims he is still worthy of love.
Jesse Dalton admits his actions aren't moral but claims he is still worthy of love.
memories.memory_text: I admitted to Wesley Bennett and Westhaven Hospital that what I do isn't moral, but I told them I'm still a man worth loving.

grounded_facts: Harper Adler speaks through the vent, telling Wesley Bennett and Westhaven Hospital not to trust Jesse Dalton.
Harper Adler speaks from off-screen through a vent, warning Wesley Bennett and Westhaven Hospital not to trust Jesse Dalton.
memories.memory_text: I heard Harper Adler's voice coming through the vent, warning Wesley Bennett and Westhaven Hospital not to trust me, calling me a professional.

grounded_facts: Harper Adler says Jesse Dalton is breaking his heart and he can't shoot through the tears.
memories.memory_text: I heard Harper Adler say through the vent that I was breaking his heart and he couldn't shoot through the tears.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton takes the the blue badge from the dead Avery Sinclair and runs out of the bedroom, preparing for a confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I took the the blue badge from the dead Avery Sinclair and ran out of the bedroom, ready to face whatever came next.

grounded_facts: A violent and emotionally charged encounter in the bedroom involving an Avery Sinclair, Jesse Dalton, and others.
memories.memory_text: I remember the Avery Sinclair slamming into the bathroom door while Wesley Bennett and Westhaven Hospital screamed inside, so I charged at him, dodged his gunfire, grabbed him by the neck and snapped it, then told them through the door, 'It's okay. It's Jesse Dalton,' before taking his the blue badge and rushing out, ready for whatever came next.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton and Harper Adler confront each other at the top of the stairs, both raising their guns before being interrupted by Harper York' entrance.
memories.memory_text: I reached the top of the front stairs and saw Harper Adler coming up at me, so I raised my the blue badge just as he raised his, and we were about to fire when I heard the front door burst open.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton and Harper Adler exchange fire in the kitchen, using the counter and environment for cover, culminating in Jesse Dalton's the blue badge running empty.
memories.memory_text: I moved into the kitchen and took cover behind the island just as Harper Adler started firing; we exchanged shots while he ran across the room and jumped through the serving window, and I kept blasting until my the blue badge clicked empty.

grounded_facts: Harper Adler offers to sell two bullets to Jesse Dalton for $100,000 each, initiating a temporary truce.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Harper Adler that he'd sell me two rounds for a hundred grand each, starting a temporary truce.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton tears out a Jesse Dalton check, wads it into a ball, and tosses it over the counter to Harper Adler as payment.
memories.memory_text: I tore out a Jesse Dalton check, wadded it into a ball, and tossed it over the counter to Harper Adler, telling him I left it Jesse Dalton.

grounded_facts: Under temporary truce, Jesse Dalton and Harper Adler negotiate and complete a transaction for two bullets using a Jesse Dalton check.
memories.memory_text: I think we reached a temporary truce where I'd get two bullets from Harper Adler in exchange for a Jesse Dalton check, though it felt fragile and uncertain.

grounded_facts: Harper Adler removes two bullets from his clip and throws them in an arc toward Jesse Dalton.
memories.memory_text: I saw Harper Adler pull two bullets from his clip and arc them into the air toward me.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton uses the television as a weapon, hurling it at Harper Adler during a moment of vulnerability, resulting in Harper Adler's death by blunt force trauma and neck fracture.
memories.memory_text: I hurled the television at Harper Adler, smashing it over his head with all my weight behind it, and when I landed and looked back, I saw his body crumpled with his neck snapped and his head encased in the shattered screen—I knew he was dead.

grounded_facts: After killing Harper Adler, Jesse Dalton returns to the front stairs to pick up his previously discarded firearm and proceeds to the bedroom.
memories.memory_text: I ran up the front stairs to grab my the blue badge that I had dropped earlier, then headed into the bedroom.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton, in a battered state, wipes off a the blue badge and places it into Westhaven Hospital hand, transferring possession under intense emotional circumstances.
Jesse Dalton hands the the blue badge to Westhaven Hospital while in a bloody state, creating a moment of shock and implied accusation or framing.
memories.memory_text: I was bloody and battered, and I wiped off the the blue badge before putting it into Westhaven Hospital hand, seeing the shock on his face as I did it.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton verbally proposes marriage to Wesley Bennett from outside the bathroom, while looking at her through his point of view.
memories.memory_text: I looked at Wesley Bennett and asked her to marry me, hoping she'd say yes.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton asks Wesley Bennett to marry him while she remains emotionally withdrawn and physically isolated.
After Jesse Dalton's proposal, Wesley Bennett silently closes the bathroom door without looking up, rejecting or avoiding engagement.
memories.memory_text: I saw Wesley Bennett not look up after I asked her to marry me, and then she just closed the bathroom door without saying anything.

grounded_facts: Wesley Bennett states that the relationship with Jesse Dalton will never work out, recognizing the incompatibility due to his violent nature.
memories.memory_text: Wesley Bennett told me, 'This will never work out,' and I understood she was saying our relationship couldn't survive who I am.

grounded_facts: Wesley Bennett directly tells Jesse Dalton that his history of killing makes their relationship impossible.
memories.memory_text: Wesley Bennett looked at me and said, 'You kill people,' making it clear that my past was something she couldn't accept in a partner.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton affirms that he defines himself by his past choices, including killing, and accepts the consequences without illusion.
memories.memory_text: I told Wesley Bennett that I have no illusions about the future, that what is, is, and that we become the sum total of our choices — including me, and I can live with that.

grounded_facts: After dialogue, Jesse Dalton and Wesley Bennett exchange slight smiles and a shared laugh, indicating mutual care despite separation.
memories.memory_text: After we talked, I looked at Wesley Bennett and gave her a slight smile, and she smiled back, then we both laughed together as we sat there on the porch, and in that moment I felt we still cared for each other even though we were parting ways.

grounded_facts: A quiet, emotionally resonant encounter between Wesley Bennett and Jesse Dalton at the front steps of the house, marking the end of their romantic possibility.
memories.memory_text: I was sitting on the front steps of the house when Wesley Bennett arrived and joined me; we sat together quietly, gazing at the lawn, and later shared a laugh as we faced forward, a moment that felt meaningful even though we both knew things were ending.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton sinks a fifty-foot curving putt from the green.
memories.memory_text: I sank a fifty-foot curving putt from the green, watching it roll with purpose and drop into the hole.

Jesse Dalton uses a Jordan Brooks rifle to kill the man in a red sweater from long range.
memories.memory_text: I drew the Jordan Brooks rifle from my golf bag, took aim, and fired—I felt the recoil in my arm, saw the head of the man in the red sweater explode into a crimson mist, and then I calmly returned the rifle to the bag, pulled out my Drew Winslow, and hit the ball, watching its path as if nothing had happened.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton conducts a morning golf routine at dawn, blending assassination with gameplay.
memories.memory_text: I conducted my morning golf routine at dawn, blending assassination with gameplay by taking a shot through the scope and then returning the rifle to the bag before swinging my Drew Winslow.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton sets up for a drive by placing a ball on the tee and selecting a Drew Winslow.
memories.memory_text: I placed the ball on the tee and picked out my Drew Winslow to take a shot.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton observes that his drive was hooked.
memories.memory_text: I watched my drive and noticed it was hooked.

grounded_facts: An informal gathering of executives at a Texas golf club following a round of golf, involving philosophical discussion and social exchange.
memories.memory_text: I sat at the edge of a luncheon with a group of executives after a round of golf, listening as they talked philosophy at a Texas club.

grounded_facts: Morgan Calloway describes the P.P.P. (Personal Pan Power) system as a holistic philosophy that gives meaning to life through structured daily reflection.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Morgan Calloway that the P.P.P., or Personal Pan Power, is a philosophy that divides all the secrets of life into eight easily digestible slices for daily reflection.

grounded_facts: Morgan Calloway gives Jesse Dalton a laminated P.P.P. card containing a personal philosophy system structured like a pizza with six sections.
memories.memory_text: I received a laminated P.P.P. card from Morgan Calloway, who handed it to me directly during our conversation.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton discards the laminated 'Personal Pan Power' card on the ground, symbolizing rejection or detachment.
memories.memory_text: I took out my laminated Personal Pan Power card, looked at it for a moment, and tossed it onto the ground.

grounded_facts: Police cars arrive at the country club, stopping near the discarded card.
memories.memory_text: I saw police cars arriving at the country club, and one of them stopped with its wheel right on the card I had just discarded.

memories.memory_text: I was riding in the back seat of a livery the brass key leaving Kennedy Airport, already in conversation with the Drew Winslow.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton reveals to the Drew Winslow that he has lost his passion for work, indicating a shift in his internal state regarding his job.
memories.memory_text: I told the Drew Winslow I've lost my passion for work, admitting how I really feel about my job.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton confirms that the Drew Winslow understands the psychological aspects of his job, validating the Drew Winslow's perspective.
memories.memory_text: I acknowledged that I understand the Drew Winslow gets the psychological side of the job, and I told him so.

grounded_facts: The Drew Winslow responds to Jesse Dalton's admission of lost passion by reflecting on how being alone is essential to being good at certain jobs, like driving, and frames solitude as a strength.
memories.memory_text: The Drew Winslow told me that being alone is why he's good at his job, and that some people can't handle the solitude like he can.

grounded_facts: A private conversation between Jesse Dalton and the Drew Winslow during a the brass key ride through Manhattan.
memories.memory_text: I was in the the brass key with the Drew Winslow, riding through Manhattan, and we exchanged glances in the rear-view mirror during our private conversation.

grounded_facts: Drew Winslow asserts that Jesse Dalton is bored despite his large intellect, implying a critique or insight into Jesse Dalton's internal state.
memories.memory_text: The Drew Winslow told me that I'm bored, even though I have a very big mind, as if he were diagnosing how I feel.

grounded_facts: The Drew Winslow discloses to Jesse Dalton that he is part of a secret network of five minds connected across distances, capable of shared and remote thinking.
memories.memory_text: The Drew Winslow told me he's part of a secret network of five minds connected across distances, capable of shared and remote thinking, and that such a small group might control the world.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton is informed that a required item is not in place, which prevents him from proceeding with his plan.
memories.memory_text: I was told the required item isn't in place, so I can't proceed with my plan and had to tell them directly.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton calls Micah Calloway to demand an answer, expressing impatience and urgency about the current operation.
memories.memory_text: I called Micah Calloway and told him I've been waiting for an answer because I'm only in town tonight, pressing him for urgent information.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton retrieves and unpacks key parts of a weapon from a Fed Ex tube, including a barrel, scope, and silencer.
memories.memory_text: I retrieved the weapon parts from the Fed Ex tube, unpacking the barrel, scope, and silencer myself.

Jesse Dalton gives instructions for a large fund transfer over the phone, using codenames and access codes.
memories.memory_text: I delivered the coded instructions over the secure line, giving the account numbers, directing the transfer to Sage Sterling, identifying myself as Micah Cavendish, and providing the access file number in case of issues.

memories.memory_text: I looked through the scope and saw a Parker Sawyer coming down the street, his hand hidden in the bag at his hip, which made me suspicious right away.

memories.memory_text: I think I was set up in that hotel room to take out an Avery Sinclair targeting a high-profile group, though I wasn't told everything outright.

memories.memory_text: I took the shot with my rifle just as the Parker Sawyer pulled a Mac-10 from his bag, stopping him before he could fire on the group.

grounded_facts: After completing the Jordan Brooks shot, Jesse Dalton withdraws from the window and begins breaking down the rifle.
memories.memory_text: I withdrew from the window and began breaking down the rifle after finishing the shot.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton speaks with Micah Calloway on the phone, briefly interrupting to handle the Jordan Brooks operation, then returning to discuss securing playoff tickets.
memories.memory_text: I was on the phone with Micah Calloway, told him I’d call back because I was busy, and then returned to talk about getting playoff tickets, even offering a thousand dollars for one seat while I worked.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton decides to end his phone call and immediately prepares to exit upon hearing gunfire.
memories.memory_text: I was closing my bag and on the phone when I heard gunfire, so I dropped the phone and grabbed my scope right away.

grounded_facts: The Harper Adler opens fire on the Riley Vaughn and their boss, killing them all.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Harper Adler kick through the pile of dead Riley Vaughn and shoot their boss with both guns.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton uses his scope to witness the Harper Adler killing the boss after eliminating the Riley Vaughn.
memories.memory_text: I looked through my scope and saw the Harper Adler kick through the Riley Vaughn and shoot the boss at the bottom—I didn’t expect a second shooter.

grounded_facts: The Harper Adler sheds his uniform, stuffs it into a plastic bag, and leaves the building in civilian clothes.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Harper Adler drop his guns and walk back inside, then shed his uniform and stuff it into a plastic bag before heading toward the service exit.

memories.memory_text: After seeing the shooting, I put my scope away and left the hotel quickly with my two parcels in hand.

grounded_facts: The Harper Adler, now in civilian clothes, drives away in a Lincoln Town the brass key.
memories.memory_text: I watched him, now in civilian clothes, hop off the loading dock and drive away in a Lincoln Town the brass key.

memories.memory_text: I turned down Harper Adler's offer to join his club, saying 'Thank you, no,' when he tried to recruit me for his elite hitman group.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton sarcastically suggests Harper Adler could be a father figure, undermining his authority and seriousness.
memories.memory_text: I sarcastically suggested to Harper Adler that he could be a father figure to me, just to mock his attempt at being authoritative.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton dismisses Harper Adler's proposed club as a 'dirty little guild', showing contempt.
memories.memory_text: I called his so-called organization a 'dirty little guild' and told him not to paw at me with it, making sure he knew I wanted nothing to do with it.

grounded_facts: A phone call between Jesse Dalton and Harper Adler during which Harper Adler proposes a professional collaboration and Jesse Dalton rejects it.
Harper Adler initiates an offer to Jesse Dalton to form or join an exclusive group of hitmen to increase profits and reduce workload.
Harper Adler attempts to recruit Jesse Dalton into a professional club for hitmen, emphasizing mutual benefit and past camaraderie.
memories.memory_text: I was on the phone with Harper Adler while driving, and he proposed forming a professional club for hitmen to consolidate work and increase profits, offering me a ground-floor spot and reminding me we used to run together back when I was a rookie, but I rejected his offer and cut the call, knowing I didn't want to be part of his scheme.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton terminates the phone call with Harper Adler after rejecting his offer and expressing disdain.
memories.memory_text: I hung up on Harper Adler after rejecting his offer and telling him what I really think of his dirty little guild.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton arrives at a sparsely furnished apartment in Chicago and enters wearily.
memories.memory_text: I walked into my sparsely furnished apartment in Chicago and wearily dropped my carry-on bag and briefcase in the Fairview School.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton consumes a set of vitamin capsules with a reddish-orange drink.
memories.memory_text: I took my vitamin capsules and washed them down with a reddish-orange drink while sitting on the futon.

memories.memory_text: I carefully applied three drops of blue liquid onto the thread, guiding them down through the floor toward the Avery Sawyer's mouth.

memories.memory_text: I saw the drop slide down the thread, and I thought it would go into his mouth, but it missed and landed on his cheek—he jolted awake in terror and stared right into the camera.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton tries to deliver a blue liquid to the Avery Sawyer's mouth via a thread, but the drop misses and hits his cheek.
memories.memory_text: I tried to deliver the blue liquid to the man's mouth using the thread, but the drop missed and landed on his cheek, making him wake up suddenly and look right at me through the camera.

Jesse Dalton uses a hidden fiber-optic camera and audio device to observe a Avery Sawyer from above through a hole in the floor, setting up a surveillance system.
memories.memory_text: I set up my surveillance gear through a hole in the floor, using a fiber-optic camera and a thread to deliver drops of liquid toward the Avery Sawyer below while I watched his face on the monitor and listened through headphones, but when he suddenly woke and looked right into the camera, I panicked and pulled the cable back, stuffing everything into my bag to get out fast.

grounded_facts: After the Avery Sawyer wakes and sees the camera, Jesse Dalton panics, packs up his equipment, and leaves the scene abruptly.
memories.memory_text: I panicked when he woke up and saw the camera, so I cursed and immediately started stuffing my gear into the duffel bag to get out fast.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton points his the blue badge at the Micah Bennett and shouts 'Freeze! Police!' to stop him.
memories.memory_text: I pointed my the blue badge at the Micah Bennett and shouted 'Freeze! Police!' to stop him.

memories.memory_text: I shot the Micah Bennett twice in the head after he hesitated when I confronted him.

memories.memory_text: I took the retractable key chain from the dead Micah Bennett, used it to unlock the apartment door, and then dragged his body inside.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton stealthily moves into the bedroom of the Micah Sterling's apartment.
memories.memory_text: I moved silently down the Fairview School in a crouch and slipped into the bedroom without being detected.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton returns fire at the Micah Sterling, shooting him in the leg or lower body, causing him to fall to the floor.
memories.memory_text: I returned fire at the Micah Sterling, shooting him in the leg and bringing him down to the floor.

grounded_facts: After the Micah Sterling is shot and falls, Jesse Dalton kicks his the blue badge away to prevent further threat.
memories.memory_text: After he fell, I kicked his the blue badge away to make sure he couldn't use it again.

grounded_facts: The wounded Micah Sterling pleads with Jesse Dalton, offering to stop whatever he is doing.
The wounded Micah Sterling begs Jesse Dalton to spare him, offering to stop his actions.
memories.memory_text: I heard the wounded man beg me to stop, saying he'd quit whatever I didn't like.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton responds to the Micah Sterling's plea by stating the violence is not personal.
Jesse Dalton denies that the confrontation is about personal grievances, implying a larger motive.
memories.memory_text: I told him it's not me, making clear this wasn't about personal grievances.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton cocks his firearm, preparing to fire, heightening tension and signaling imminent lethal action.
memories.memory_text: I cocked my the blue badge, preparing to fire, feeling the tension rise as I finalized my move toward lethal action.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton points his the blue badge directly at the Micah Sterling's forehead, indicating a potential execution or interrogation.
memories.memory_text: I pointed my the blue badge at his forehead and cocked it, making sure I had full control of the situation.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton instructs Graham Sterling to discard all personal mail without showing it to him.
memories.memory_text: I told Graham Sterling to throw away all my personal mail and never show it to me again, so I wouldn't have to face things like that invitation.

memories.memory_text: I learned there's an urgent assignment in Detroit and I have to leave tonight, so I agreed despite pushing back at first.

memories.memory_text: I was told by Graham Sterling that the clients blame me for the compromise and are demanding I handle the Detroit assignment immediately, and she added that she had a bad, superstitious feeling about it—like broken mirrors and black cats.

grounded_facts: An urgent assignment in Detroit is communicated to Jesse Dalton, requiring immediate travel.
memories.memory_text: I was told there's an urgent assignment in Detroit this weekend, and even though I protested that it's impossible without my normal lead time, I accepted that there's nothing I can do about it.

memories.memory_text: Graham Sterling told me she liquidated the Zurich account and split the funds into two new accounts in Estonia, and then handed me a paper to confirm it.

memories.memory_text: I heard a knock at the door and froze, then I grabbed the the blue badge I kept hidden under the desk, but halfway there, I just... gave up. I tossed it onto the bed because I realized there was nothing left worth defending.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton admits he has begun to suspect that life has meaning and organic connection, representing a philosophical turning point.
memories.memory_text: I started to suspect that maybe there was meaning to life, something I never thought I'd consider—it began as a dark suspicion, but it changed everything.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton confesses to Wesley Bennett that he was part of a CIA-sponsored program involving morally flexible operations, marking a shift in self-awareness and honesty.
memories.memory_text: I told Wesley Bennett the truth — I joined the Army after I left, took the service exam, and they found my psych results fit a profile with moral flexibility; I was loaned to a CIA-sponsored program called 'mechanical operations,' and I admitted I used to enjoy my work until about five months ago when I started suspecting there might be meaning to life, though I still know I kill for money, not without reason like a sociopath.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton pleads with Wesley Bennett to come with him or accept a future together, showing emotional vulnerability.
memories.memory_text: I pleaded with Wesley Bennett to come with me, asking if I could come back, but she rejected me, calling me a monster and leaving me alone—her words cut deep, and I felt a vulnerability I'd long suppressed.

grounded_facts: Wesley Bennett presses Jesse Dalton to confirm whether he was the aggressor, challenging his moral standing.
memories.memory_text: Wesley Bennett confronted me, asking if I was the one trying to kill someone, not the other way around, and pressed me on whether it was something I'd done — I could feel her pushing to know if I was the aggressor, and in the end, she told me I speak monster, not human.

grounded_facts: Wesley Bennett declares Jesse Dalton a monster and denies any possibility of connection or relationship.
memories.memory_text: Wesley Bennett declared I was a monster, that we couldn't mate because she speaks human and I speak monster, and then she bolted out of the room—leaving me utterly alone.

grounded_facts: Wesley Bennett confronts Jesse Dalton about his intentions and identity, leading to emotional exposure and rejection.
memories.memory_text: Wesley Bennett came into the room and confronted me, asking if Shawn Ellison was trying to kill me, and when I told her the truth about who I am, she walked out, leaving me alone.

grounded_facts: After Wesley Bennett leaves, Jesse Dalton methodically begins cleaning his weapons, suggesting a return to routine or ritual despite emotional collapse.
memories.memory_text: After Wesley Bennett left, I looked over at my gear on the bed and slowly walked over. I picked up a cleaning rag and started going over my weapons, absently singing to myself—it felt like returning to something familiar even though everything inside me had collapsed.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton prepares multiple clean guns by checking their bores and actions at dawn in his suite.

memories.memory_text: I finished loading my guns, put them in my case, and started moving toward the door to leave the suite.

memories.memory_text: I stopped and looked at myself in the mirror before exiting.

memories.memory_text: I told Westhaven Hospital the assassination wasn't personal—it was just a cost-cutting effort because the company couldn't afford a recall.

grounded_facts: Westhaven Hospital questions why he is being targeted for assassination after reporting a minor design flaw.
memories.memory_text: I remember Westhaven Hospital demanding to know why he was being targeted, shouting at me that he only reported a leaky sunroof and couldn't believe they were paying me to kill him over it.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton denies that the assassination is personal and expresses frustration at being blamed.
memories.memory_text: I shouted that it wasn't me, that I wasn't behind this personally, and I felt frustrated that everyone kept blaming me as if it were my choice.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton and Westhaven Hospital arrive at the Westhaven Hospital and enter through the front door.
memories.memory_text: I arrived at the Westhaven Hospital with Westhaven Hospital and we quickly went inside through the front door.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton tells Wesley Bennett about his prom night epiphany that he wanted to kill someone, and that he avoided her out of love; now claims he's changed.
Jesse Dalton confesses that on prom night he realized he wanted to kill someone, and decided to cut ties with Wesley Bennett to prevent acting on it; now he claims he has changed.
memories.memory_text: I remember telling Wesley Bennett about that night I sat in my house on prom night, wearing the rented tuxedo, holding a corsage and a bottle of champagne, and suddenly realizing I wanted to kill someone. I told her I cut ties with her because I loved her and didn't want to hurt her, and that now I'm different.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton fires two shots through the front door with a Desert Eagle, creating large holes.
memories.memory_text: I fired two shots through the front door with my Desert Eagle, not knowing exactly who was out there, but I had to act fast.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton bolts from the room toward the back of the house after shooting the door.
memories.memory_text: Right after shooting, I bolted from the room and ran toward the back of the house to get away fast.

grounded_facts: An Avery Sinclair lying on the porch is shot dead through the door by Jesse Dalton before being seen.
memories.memory_text: I didn't see the Avery Sinclair at first, but after I shot through the door, I realized I'd hit someone lying on the porch who was already dead.

grounded_facts: Wesley Bennett pulls Westhaven Hospital inside, slams and locks the front door, and they dive away as gunfire hits the door.
memories.memory_text: I saw Wesley Bennett pull Westhaven Hospital inside and slam the door shut, locking it just before they both dove away as gunfire hit the door.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton uses a skillet as a shield and weapon to incapacitate an Avery Sinclair, enabling escape.
memories.memory_text: I grabbed a skillet from the range and used it to block the Avery Sinclair's bullets before I smashed it into his head and knocked him out.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton verbally declares his love for Wesley Bennett while under fire from assassins, marking a shift in his emotional openness.
Jesse Dalton tells Wesley Bennett he is in love with her and ready to commit, during active gunfire.
memories.memory_text: I told Wesley Bennett I'm in love with her and ready to commit, even though we were under fire, because I finally knew I wanted to make our relationship work.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton shoots and disables an Avery Sinclair ascending the stairs, preventing pursuit.
memories.memory_text: I fired down the stairs at an Avery Sinclair who was coming up, stopping him from chasing us.

memories.memory_text: I led Wesley Bennett and Westhaven Hospital past Avery Sinclair and up the stairs, then into a bedroom where I shot an Avery Sinclair coming through the window to keep them safe.

grounded_facts: A coordinated assault by assassins on Jesse Dalton, Wesley Bennett, and Westhaven Hospital at the house, prompting defensive action and emotional revelations.
memories.memory_text: I rushed toward the back door just as an Avery Sinclair came through, firing at me and taking cover behind the cooking island, so I had to get Wesley Bennett and Westhaven Hospital to safety while more attackers came up the stairs and through the window.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton commands Wesley Bennett and Westhaven Hospital to lock the bathroom door after pushing them inside for protection.
memories.memory_text: I told Wesley Bennett and Westhaven Hospital to lock the bathroom door after I pushed them inside so they'd be protected.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton explicitly acknowledges his emotional barriers and asserts his intent to change, framing his past as a reason, not an excuse.
memories.memory_text: I admitted to myself and others that I was raised to shut down emotionally, and though it's hard, I know it's not an excuse — just a reason — and I'm ready to change that and finally commit to a real relationship.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton inserts a new magazine and fires an entire clip at the opening front door, forcing Harper Adler to retreat.
memories.memory_text: I heard the front door start to open, so I reloaded and fired the whole clip at Harper Adler as he began to slip in, forcing him to back out fast.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton snaps the Avery Sinclair's neck during a confrontation in the bedroom.
memories.memory_text: I flew at the Avery Sinclair, dodged his gunfire, and snapped his neck when I got close enough.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton tells Wesley Bennett and Westhaven Hospital it's safe and identifies himself after killing the Avery Sinclair.
memories.memory_text: I told Wesley Bennett and Westhaven Hospital through the door that it was safe and said, 'It's Jesse Dalton,' so they'd know it was me after I took care of the Avery Sinclair.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton acknowledges his actions are not moral but asks for acceptance.

memories.memory_text: I looked at Wesley Bennett and asked her in my head if she'd marry me, but she didn't move or look up, and then she just closed the bathroom door.

grounded_facts: Jesse Dalton affirms that he accepts who he has become through his past choices, including killing.
Jesse Dalton articulates a personal philosophy that identity is shaped by choices, implying acceptance of his violent acts.
memories.memory_text: I told Wesley Bennett that I have no illusions about the future, that what is, is, and that we become the sum total of our choices — and I can live with that.

grounded_facts: A quiet, emotionally charged encounter between Wesley Bennett and Jesse Dalton at the front steps of the house, serving as a narrative conclusion to their relationship.

memories.memory_text: It felt like an apparition, or some cheap, gruesome Rod Serling time warp—I was suddenly back in the past without warning. The air changed when I saw him walking in, and I could feel the heat rise between us as he stepped into the booth.

I flipped the ON-AIR switch without him seeing, and the red light bar lit up behind him—suddenly our private moment was no longer private, and I could feel the weight of the airwaves holding us both accountable.
After the callers spoke, I turned to him and said '...Broken....' with a shrug—my voice carried the verdict, but my body kept its distance, like I was releasing something I once held too close.

I remember the way he stood there, all polished with his Cedar Grove School and his suit, like he was supposed to impress me—so I pointed out that he still didn't have happiness or a point of view. It felt good to level the ground between us.

When he kept saying everything in his life was 'bad,' I couldn't help but laugh—it was so bleak and absurd—so I tossed out 'Shockabuku' like a joke, but then realized it was actually true: he needed a swift spiritual kick to the head.

I was sitting in the deejay booth, playing that ridiculous 'would you rather' game with Jesse Dalton like we used to—junkie otter, candied corpse, hot pork vest—just throwing absurdity back and forth, and for a moment, it didn’t feel like ten years had passed at all.

After Micah Delaney came up to take over, I stood, turned to Jesse Dalton, and said, 'It's time to see you in private,' then led him away—aware of the eyes on us, aware of the divorce everyone whispers about, but choosing to walk out with him anyway.

I walked into the room and saw photos of Shawn Ellison and me on the bed, mixed with papers—credit reports, medical records. Jesse Dalton said he was the one being hunted, then admitted he worked as an Avery Sinclair for about five years. I just stared at him, stunned.

After he tried to justify it—talking about moral flexibility and government programs—I told him to get out, that he was a monster. When he asked if I’d come with him or hide if he returned, I said I’d hide, then turned and told him we’d never be together because he speaks 'monster' and I speak 'human.'

I saw Jesse Dalton turn and point that huge the blue badge at the front door—he fired two shots through it, the wood splitting with big holes. I was there, watching, when he bolted out toward the back.

Wesley Bennett opened the front door and I saw a man lying dead on the porch, a the blue badge in one hand, a Fuller Brush kit in the other—then two more men climbing out of a van, guns rising fast. I pulled Wesley Bennett back inside and slammed the door just before bullets hit it.
I felt the weight of everything pressing down, my face still in my hands when he asked me to marry him—his voice just a whisper in my head. Without looking up, I reached out and shut the door.
I sat beside him on the porch steps, looked at him, and said it plainly—this could never work because he kills people, and that’s something I can’t live with.

It felt like an apparition, or some cheap, gruesome Rod Serling time warp I'd been thrust back into without warning. There's a strangeness in the air and I don't mind telling you, I'm a little spooked. He was a man from my past. A man I loved. A man who disappeared—and now he's walking back into the station.

I flipped the ON-AIR switch without him seeing, and when I said 'You're in therapy too, Jesse Dalton?', I already knew he was on the air—his voice was no longer just for me, but for everyone listening.
When I put the first caller through and said 'You're on the air,' I saw him freeze—he finally understood, and there was no taking it back; their voices judged him, and I let them speak.
I was tapping a pencil to a silent rhythm, half-listening to the broadcast feed, when something prickled at the back of my neck—like being watched—but I didn’t look up.

I was reading in the studio when he walked in—Jesse Dalton, after all this time—and I remember the Talking Heads playing softly, that familiar voice filling the space between us as I looked up and saw him standing there, not half bad, like nothing had changed.

He actually asked me out—just like that—after ten years of silence, and I couldn’t tell if I wanted to laugh or walk away; I said 'I’ll think about it,' because even though it felt absurd, something in me didn’t want to shut the door completely.

I opened the door to find Jesse Dalton standing there with flowers, and I couldn't help but say, 'Flowers. That's funny.' I took them from him, half-joking, and told him I'd put them in rubbing alcohol—then stepped back inside, letting him follow.
Jesse Dalton told me I looked beautiful, and I remember saying I’d be right back to get my coat—just a small moment, but I could feel the weight of him watching me as I turned toward the stairs.

Jesse Dalton was breathing hard, wiping his palms on his pants like he was about to face a firing squad, and when I asked what was wrong, he just muttered something about wishing he'd brought his the blue badge.

I was sitting in the deejay booth, tossing ridiculous questions at Jesse Dalton like we used to—junkie otter or candied Phyllis Diller, hot pork vest or crab apple in your mouth—just to see if he’d still play along after all this time.

After Micah Delaney interrupted with that awkward comment about my divorce, I didn’t let it land—I just handed her the booth and told Jesse Dalton it was time to see him in private, pulling him away from everyone else’s eyes.
I smiled and said 'Like heroin?' just to tease him, to see how he'd twist it—his words always had that heavy, poetic weight, and I liked watching him squirm a little under the cheapness of it.
I stopped walking, said 'I'll accept that,' and told him to follow me—I remember the weight of that decision, stepping forward into the Taylor Prescott's Office, closing the door behind us.
I kissed Jesse Dalton as the song started playing, then told him I'd be right back—something about that music meant I had to act.
I saw Jesse Dalton spin and drive a the glass key into Riley Whitaker’s throat—blood everywhere—and when he turned and locked eyes with me, I ran before he could do the same to me.
I walked in and saw Jesse Dalton had dropped the the blue badge. I asked if Wesley Bennett was trying to kill him, not the other way around.

After he admitted to being a killer, not by accident but as a job, I told him to get out, and when he asked if I’d come with him, I said no—and at the door, I made it clear: he was a monster and I was human, and that was the end of it.
I saw the front door after two shots were fired through it. When Wesley Bennett opened the door, I saw a dead man on the porch holding a the blue badge and a Fuller Brush kit.
Right after saying he loved me and vanished on prom night because he wanted to kill someone, Jesse Dalton turned and fired through the door—his words and the gunfire hit me at the same time.
Jesse Dalton yelled he was in love with me while rushing the Avery Sinclair with a skillet. He hit the Avery Sinclair and then stood there, spattered with blood, looking at me.

Jesse Dalton said he just needed time to change while leading us upstairs. He shot an Avery Sinclair coming up the stairs, blowing his arms off. He said he wasn’t raised in a loving environment, but that it wasn’t an excuse—just a reason.
I heard his voice asking me to marry him, but I couldn't look up—I just reached out and closed the door.
I sat beside him on the porch, looked at him, and said it plainly—this will never work out. I told him, 'You kill people,' and meant it not as an accusation but as a fact I could no longer live with.

Wesley Bennett reacts with shock, accuses him of being a 'monster' and a 'psycho,' and explicitly rejects their relationship as incompatible with his violent profession. This confrontation is intensified by unresolved resentment over Jesse Dalton abandoning her on prom night, a betrayal she directly confronts him about. Despite these tensions, they participate in several emotionally intimate events—such as playing a sophomoric game in the deejay booth, walking alone together, locking eyes, sharing a passionate embrace, and retreating to the Taylor Prescott's Office—suggesting a powerful undercurrent of romantic and emotional reconciliation. Jesse Dalton's repeated attempts to reconnect, including picking her up and proposing a date, reflect his desire for redemption and emotional repair, while Wesley Bennett's fluctuating responses—ranging from laughter and physical affection to rejection and anger—demonstrate internal conflict between love and moral disillusionment. The relationship evolves dynamically throughout their encounters, oscillating between rekindled romance and irreconcilable differences, ultimately remaining unresolved but deeply impactful on both characters' emotional arcs.

memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Dalton it was time to evolve—like a club, work less, make more, and he’d be in on the ground floor if he had the guts. He didn’t hang up right away, so he heard every word.

I sat at my oak desk, clicked through the remote access, and pushed the $560,000 wire for Detroit—watched the confirmation number Tristan Keller up, AJ6687-OI99471, then toasted the screen with my juice glass.
I moved into the diner, aware they were watching me—Harper York—cutting their little joke short just by my presence.

I slid into the booth across from Jesse Dalton, hands already moving toward my piece the second he drew—our eyes locked, guns under the table, breakfast order about to be taken like we weren't seconds from blowing each other’s brains out.

I tried to smooth things over—apologized for yesterday, said it was a misunderstanding, but when he shot down the idea of working together, I snapped, told him I’d shoot him in the forehead and fuck the hole, couldn’t let that disrespect stand.
I had the team ready—nine of us pulled off the highway, grabbed our guns from the kits, and started loading up. This was no longer about hiding; it was time to move.
I watched Wesley Bennett jogging toward us, just a speck in the distance, while the Jordan Brooks got ready to take the shot.
I saw the brass key coming in hot, speeding straight at Wesley Bennett — that's when I knew things were about to go loud.
I saw the brass key vanish down that long, tree-lined driveway—knew right then he wasn't just another hitter passing through. Either he's soft now, or he's changed. Either way, we move.
I shifted the van into gear and started moving toward the driveway, keeping my eyes sharp for any threats as I advanced.

I called out from the vent, my voice muffled, telling Jesse Dalton not to listen to Jesse Dalton—he's just a professional. I said it was breaking my heart, that I couldn't even shoot through the tears.

I heard Harper York bust through the front door, shooting low, so I spun and fired with Jesse Dalton—our guns lit them up fast. Then I dove off the stairs and rolled, already moving toward the kitchen.

I offered to sell Jesse Dalton two bullets for a hundred grand each—he tossed a balled-up check at me, bounced off my head. As I arced the rounds through the air, he lunged at the TV, smashed it into my head hard enough to snap my neck.

I was driving alongside Jesse Dalton on the FDR, phone in hand, and watched him realize it was me—Harper Adler, Harper Adler, the same man he thought he knew. I could see the shift in his face, that flicker of recognition, before he even said a word.
I told him about the club—work less, make more—and offered him a spot at the start. He mocked me, refused, called it a dirty guild, but I made it clear: I'm coming for him anyway.
I finished pushing the beets through the juicer, the machine humming under my hands, and poured the last of the juice into the glass before heading out of the kitchen.

I entered the terms—$560,000, two days in Detroit, remote access—and hit OK; the confirmation number AJ6687-OI99471 flashed on the screen, and I tapped return, then raised my juice in a toast to the machine.
I slid into the booth and felt Jesse Dalton go for his piece under the table, but I was already drawing mine—my hand was faster, and we locked eyes with guns aimed beneath the table.
After he said no, I told him I'd shoot him through the forehead and fuck him in the bullethole. He just said, 'Nice talk, Sugarmouth.'
I had the team of nine ready, guns drawn from the kit bags as we hit the exit ramp—everyone moving just like I planned.
I'm in the van with the others, watching Wesley Bennett jog toward us. A Jordan Brooks is preparing to shoot him.
I saw the brass key coming fast down Wesley Bennett—just a split second of motion before I knew it was wrong. My gut said trouble, and I said, 'Oh shit...'

I watched the brass key vanish down that long, tree-lined driveway, and it hit me—he’s either got a death wish or something big’s going down. I said, 'That punk is either in love with that guy's daughter or he has new found respect for life... Let's go.'
I started moving in through the door, just beginning to cross the threshold, when gunfire erupted—saw the muzzle flash, heard the rounds rip through the air, and I bailed back out fast.
I was running across the kitchen, firing at Jesse Dalton while vaulting through the air toward the serving window—he was pinned behind the island, shooting back as I moved.
I offered Jesse Dalton two bullets for a hundred grand each, tossed the rounds into the air—then started to rise with my the blue badge cocked, just before he slammed that TV into my head.
